one_month_reasoning: No NVDA earnings in the window: Q3 FY27 reports 2026-11-17 (after 11-04). Scheduled drivers inside the window: late-October hyperscaler results and 2027 capex guides (MSFT, GOOGL, META, AMZN), where Meta and Microsoft already flagged memory/component pricing inflating capex; a 2027 capex raise is supportive, digestion language is the main downside risk. The FOMC meets Oct 27-28 (decision Oct 28; corrected from 'early November' per supervisor), with prediction markets pricing ~17% odds of an October hike and ~75% for December, so a hawkish surprise is a modest multiple risk. Stock sits at its 52-week high with momentum, partly offset by mild reversal risk. Net: essentially symmetric around spot (median ~+0.3%) at slightly above usual monthly vol (38%/3.5 x 1.08 = ~11.7%) for the capex-print cluster; unchanged from round 1.

fair_value.method: Blend of 16x consistent-basis NTM EPS at Oct-2027 (Q3 FY28-Q2 FY29 ~$17.5) = $280 (60%) and a 5.0% FCF yield on ~$300B NTM FCF plus $57B of net cash and haircut equity stakes over 23.8B shares = $255 (40%); blended ~$270. Break-even multiple on $17.5 is 13.5x, so 16x already absorbs ~17% further de-rating from today's 19.3-19.5x.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: Consistent NTM EPS at Oct-2027 (Q3 FY28-Q2 FY29) ~$17.5 x 16x; break-even 13.5x

inputs_detail.derivation: Consensus $15.68 (range $9.80-$18.75). Cross-checked bottom-up: FY27 revenue ~$404B (Q1 $81.6B + Q2 $96.2B + Q3 guide $108B + Q4 ~$118B) x 1.70 per management's ~70% FY28 growth guide = ~$686B; GM 72.5% (FY28 guide 72-73%); opex ~$50B; tax 17%; ~23.9B diluted shares = ~$15.6.

Sharp deceleration from +70% because FY28 is supply-constrained and hyperscaler capex already guided to ~$1.3T in 2027 with FCF thinning (Meta) and component inflation (MSFT/Meta) absorbing budget; Wells Fargo capex-math caution cited in source 9.

inputs_detail.input: NTM EPS at 2027-10-05 (Q3 FY28 + Q4 FY28 + Q1 FY29 + Q2 FY29)
inputs_detail.derivation: Same window construction as today's 19.3x (next four unreported quarters). H2 FY28 = FY28 $15.7 - Q1 FY28 $3.17 - Q2 FY28 $3.63 = $8.90 (quarterly consensus, source 12); H1 FY29 ~$8.6-8.9 assuming FY29 +15% with quarters flattening off the Q4 FY28 run-rate. Total ~$17.5 (supervisor range $17.4-17.8 for FY29 +10-20%). Round 1 used Q4 FY28-Q3 FY29, one quarter shifted.

Below NVDA's current ~19.3-19.5x on the same NTM basis and far below the peer median ~35x: by Oct-2027 forward growth decelerates from +70% toward ~15%, and the market prices peak-cycle risk (MU at 6x is the extreme). Inside the 6-129x peer range; below AVGO/TSM ~20.5x because NVDA's post-FY28 growth is more cyclical and customer-concentrated. Break-even is 13.5x ($236.88/$17.5), so 16x embeds ~2.5 turns of further compression but not a 31% de-rating. Kept at 16x rather than the supervisor's 16.5x: compression has been estimate-driven so far, but by the horizon the estimates themselves will be decelerating, removing that support.

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: NTM FCF ~$300B (72% of ~$416B NI) at 5.0% yield + $23.2B net cash + $34.2B haircut equity stakes, 23.8B shares

inputs_detail.derivation: H1 FY27 FCF $69.9B vs non-GAAP NI ~$99B (~70%); Q2 alone $21.3B FCF vs $54.0B non-GAAP NI as receivables jumped to $63.1B (DSO 60 vs 45) and inventory to $31.6B. Assume modest improvement to 72%.

Cash $22.443B + marketable debt securities $34.143B - debt $33.366B ($1.0B short-term + $32.366B long-term) per 10-Q balance sheet. Round 1 wrongly included $42.8B of marketable equity securities as cash.

10-Q: marketable equity securities $42.783B (Level 1 $31.977B publicly held; Level 2 $10.806B unregistered warrants/preferred; $36.9B under short-term lock-ups, $5.0B locked through Dec-2027) at a 50% haircut = $21.4B; non-marketable equity securities $51.157B at a 75% haircut = $12.8B. Haircuts reflect lock-ups, AI-valuation volatility and that some stakes are in customers (circularity).

AVGO and TSM trade ~20.5x forward EPS (~4.9% earnings yield). At 72% conversion a 16x P/E corresponds to a 4.5% FCF yield; I require 5.0% (~13.9x P/E equivalent) because the cash leg should carry the working-capital and receivables-concentration risk (DSO 60, terms up to one year), which is why this leg sits below the P/E leg.
24.285B diluted Q2 FY27 less ~400M/yr repurchased (203M in H1 FY27) plus SBC dilution.

bear.story: 2027 brings capex digestion signals (2028 hyperscaler capex flat), memory-cost squeeze takes GM to ~70%, receivables/financing worries grow and equity stakes mark down; consistent-basis NTM EPS falls to ~$14 (FY29 down) and the market pays ~10.5x. About 8.3x today's consensus horizon EPS.

base.story: FY28 roughly delivers ~$15.5-16 EPS on the Rubin ramp (+70% revenue, GM 72-73%, verified in the call transcript); growth visibly decelerates into FY29 so the multiple compresses to ~15.5x on ~$17.5 consistent NTM EPS; stock grinds up ~13%.

bull.story: Demand stays above supply into 2028, horizon NTM EPS rises to ~$20 (FY29 +25%+), receivables normalize and the market holds ~18.5x, still below AVGO/TSM today.

comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: 16x NTM EPS at Oct-2027, inside the range but in the bottom third and below NVDA's own current ~19.3x NTM (stockanalysis) / ~17x (24/7 Wall St, 2026-09-28).
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: Discount to the median, not a premium. NVDA's FY28 growth (~70% revenue) is far above peers, but the multiple is applied to Oct-2027 NTM earnings when growth is expected to slow sharply; earnings are at a probable cyclical high with five customers holding 70% of receivables, extended payment terms up to one year, $279B supply commitments (mostly memory) and $25B committed equity investments in its own ecosystem. MU at 6x shows how the market prices peak-cycle AI earnings. Forward EV/EBITDA for peers is approximated as trailing EV/EBITDA x (forward P/E / trailing P/E).

thesis_break_reason: $145 (~-39%, ~8.3x consistent-basis Oct-2027 NTM EPS of $17.5 and ~9x FY28 consensus, below the 52-week low of $164) would imply the market expects FY29 earnings to fall materially: hyperscaler capex cuts, order push-outs that strand the $279B supply commitments, a credit problem in the extended-term receivables, or the $105B lease-guarantee cap being called. Ordinary 38% vol rarely takes a name 25% below its 52-week low without a fundamental break.

key_uncertainties: Durability past FY28: today's 19.3-19.5x NTM (Q3 FY27-Q2 FY28, $12.00-12.25) is a decade low; a flat year needs only ~13.5x on $17.5 horizon EPS, so the outcome turns on EPS delivery, not re-rating. FY28 EPS range $9.80-$18.75 shows wide disagreement.
Working capital: receivables $63.1B (DSO 60 vs 45 prior quarter), payment terms up to one year, five customers = 70% of receivables; Q2 OCF $24.1B vs non-GAAP NI $54.0B.
Supply commitments jumped to $279B from $119B, mostly memory; GM guided down to 71-72% in Q4 and 72-73% in FY28.
Customer financing/circularity: $25B of committed future equity investments, $23.7B of H1 equity gains flowing through GAAP EPS.
Hyperscaler capex affordability (Meta FCF thinning, component inflation) and custom-ASIC share (AVGO, MRVL).
Equity stakes: $42.8B marketable plus $51.2B non-marketable equity securities (10-Q), mostly AI-ecosystem companies under lock-ups; marks flow through GAAP EPS and are not cash.
reasoning: Round 2. Primary documents show an extraordinary ramp: Q2 FY27 revenue $96.2B (+106% y/y), non-GAAP EPS $2.22, Q3 guide $108B, and a call guide of ~70% FY28 revenue growth, supply-constrained, with GM settling at 72-73% (verified verbatim by the supervisor). Bottom-up FY28 EPS ~$15.6 matches consensus $15.7. The supervisor found two errors that I verified and fixed: (1) net cash is $23.2B, not $66B: I re-read the 10-Q balance sheet and $42.8B of 'marketable securities' are equity stakes (Level 1 $32.0B, Level 2 $10.8B, mostly locked up); I now add them separately at a 50% haircut, plus non-marketable stakes ($51.2B) at 75%; (2) my horizon NTM EPS was shifted one quarter; on the consistent Q3 FY28-Q2 FY29 window (verified quarterly consensus $2.47/$2.73/$3.17/$3.63 for the current NTM, so H2 FY28 = $8.90) it is ~$17.5, slightly above my round-1 $17.3 because my round-1 build had decelerated quarters too sharply. Today's 19.3x is on $12.00-12.25; the 17x and 14.8x quotes are later windows, so I compress from 19.3x not 17x. I keep 16x (not the supervisor's 16.5x) because by the horizon estimate growth itself decelerates; break-even is 13.5x, so 16x embeds ~2.5 turns of compression. Fair value $270 (+14%), up from $267: the EPS-window fix (+$3 on P/E leg) outweighs the net-cash cut (-$1.8/share before adding back haircut stakes). Scenarios 145/268/370 at 25/50/25 (mean ~$263). Ladder is a 50/50 blend of a lognormal (median $253, sigma 0.42, above 38% realized vol for cycle/event risk) and a scenario mixture, with fat left tail kept: P(>= spot) 59.4%. No option data used; priors not opened.
